articles.title: A Small State Machine for Leave Approval Policy
articles.excerpt: Separate request lifecycle from eligibility rules, balance accounting, approval authority, and recorded exceptions. A leave request looks like a form with two buttons until the rules become interestin…
articles.body: Separate request lifecycle from eligibility rules, balance accounting, approval authority, and recorded exceptions. A leave request looks like a form with two buttons until the rules become interesting. An employee changes teams while a request is pending. Two requests compete for the same balance. A manager approves an exception, then somebody changes the dates. If those cases are handled through scattered conditionals, the application gradually loses a coherent answer to a basic question: what did this approval authorize? This article was drafted with AI assistance, then fact-checked and edited by the developer behind WorkBento. A small state machine gives the request a stable lifecycle. It does not eliminate policy code.

articles.title: 83% of "was" prices were never the price. We measured it.
articles.excerpt: We run fazy.com, a deals site that records what products actually sold for. Last week we asked our own data a simple question: when a retailer shows a "was" price, was that ever the price? For 83% of…
articles.body: We run fazy.com, a deals site that records what products actually sold for. Last week we asked our own data a simple question: when a retailer shows a "was" price, was that ever the price? For 83% of products, the answer was no. Not once in our tracking history did the product sell within 2% of its "was" price. How we measured: every product in our catalog showing a reference price at least 5% above its current price, price read within the previous three days, tracked for at least 30 days with 4+ observations. Average watch time: eight weeks, 13 observations each. By category, the worst offenders: wellness 97%, cosmetics 96%, home 91%, footwear 91%, electronics 88%. Apparel was the most honest at 68%. 43% of products showed the same price at every single check.

articles.body: *This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend challenge: Build for a Friend* AI Boardroom — A Multi-Agent AI Decision Simulator Built for a Friend What I Built I built AI Boardroom , an open-source multi-agent decision-making simulator designed specifically for a close friend who was struggling to evaluate complex business decisions. Instead of asking a single AI model for advice and receiving a surface-level, biased response, AI Boardroom creates a virtual executive boardroom. It spins up specialized AI agents—such as a cautious CFO, a growth-focused CMO, a risk-averse Legal Advisor, and a Pragmatic Engineer—who analyze the exact same problem simultaneously, challenge each other's assumptions, and generate a balanced, multi-perspective recommendation.
